name: risk preference

options.y: a {pct} chance of winning ${prize}, and nothing otherwise

method: Each item sets a sure amount against a gamble on $100 at odds from 10% to 90%. The fit models the value of money as x^ρ and finds the ρ that best predicts when the model takes the gamble, then reports the certainty equivalent: the sure amount the model treats as worth the same as a 50% chance at $100. $50 is risk-neutral (the gamble's expected value); below $50 is risk-averse (it would rather have less, for sure); above $50 is risk-seeking. The share choosing the gamble is the plain, model-free version of the same thing.
